# Digitized Montana Newspapers

The Montana Historical Society retired its Montana Newspapers website (montananewspapers.org). Users visiting that website will be redirected here. All content previously available on Montana Newspapers is now accessible through our Public Access Portal.  Our digitized newspapers are available online via our [Public Access Portal](https://mthspublic.newspapers.com/?odt=GGudNFWGwotbNfAmdZcGYQ%3D%3D), [Chronicling America](https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/), and various other sites. We have the most digitized newspapers available through our Onsite Portal, accessed in-person at the Library & Archives Reference Room. 
View our newspapers index, available as a PDF or XLSX, to find out what newspapers are available and where to access them.

**Sedro-Woolley** ([/ˌ s iː d r oʊ ˈ w ʊ l i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_SEE-droh WUUL-ee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")) is a city in [Skagit County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_County,_Washington "Skagit County, Washington"), [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)"), United States. It is part of the [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon,_Washington "Mount Vernon, Washington")–[Anacortes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anacortes,_Washington "Anacortes, Washington"), Washington [Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "Metropolitan Statistical Area") and had a population of 12,421 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). The city is home to the administrative offices of [North Cascades National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Cascades_National_Park "North Cascades National Park"), which lies east of Sedro-Woolley on [State Route 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_20 "Washington State Route 20").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Sedro-Woolley%2C_Washington_%281906%29.jpg/330px-Sedro-Woolley%2C_Washington_%281906%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sedro-Woolley,_Washington_(1906).jpg)

Sedro-Woolley in 1906

Incorporated on December 19, 1898, Sedro-Woolley was formed from neighboring rival towns of Sedro (once known as Bug) and Woolley in [Skagit County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_County "Skagit County"), northwestern Washington, 25 miles (40 kilometres) inland from [Puget Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puget_Sound "Puget Sound"), 40 miles (64 kilometres) south of the border with Canada and 65 miles (105 kilometres) north of [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-5)

Four British bachelors, led by David Batey, homesteaded the area in 1878, the time logjam obstructions were cleared downriver at the site of Mount Vernon.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-6) In 1884–85, Batey built a store and home for the Mortimer Cook family from [Santa Barbara, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara,_California "Santa Barbara, California") where Cook had been mayor for two terms. Cook intended to name his new Pacific Northwest town Bug due to the number of [mosquitoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquitoes "Mosquitoes") present, but his wife protested along with a handful of other local wives. Cook was already the namesake for the town Cook's Ferry on the Thompson River in [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"). With "Bug" being so unpopular, Cook derived a town name from Spanish; knowing ["cedro"](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedrus "es:Cedrus") was the word for cedar, he replaced one letter to make the name unique, settling on "Sedro".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-7)

Sedro, on the northern banks of the [Skagit River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_River "Skagit River"), proved susceptible to floods. In 1889, [Northern Pacific Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Pacific_Railway "Northern Pacific Railway") developer [Nelson Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Bennett "Nelson Bennett") began laying track from the town of [Fairhaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairhaven,_Washington "Fairhaven, Washington"), 25 miles (40 kilometres) northwest on [Bellingham Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellingham_Bay "Bellingham Bay"), and real estate developer Norman R. Kelley platted a new town of Sedro on high ground a mile northwest of Cook's site. The [Fairhaven and Southern Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairhaven_and_Southern_Railroad "Fairhaven and Southern Railroad") arrived in Sedro on Christmas Eve, 1889, in time for Bennett to receive a performance bonus from the towns at both ends, and a month after Washington became the 42nd state in the Union.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-8)

Within months, two more railroads crossed the F&S roadbed a half mile north of new Sedro, forming a triangle where 11 trains eventually arrived daily. Railroad developer [Philip A. Woolley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley "Philip Woolley") moved his family from [Elgin, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgin,_Illinois "Elgin, Illinois"), to Sedro in December 1899 and bought land around the triangle. He built the Skagit River Lumber & Shingle Mill next to where the railroads crossed and he started his namesake company town there that was based on sales of railroad ties to the three rail companies, including the [Seattle and Northern Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_and_Northern_Railway?action=edit&redlink=1 "Seattle and Northern Railway (page does not exist)") (forerunner of the [Great Northern Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Northern_Railway_(U.S.) "Great Northern Railway (U.S.)")) and the [Northern Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Pacific_Railroad "Northern Pacific Railroad").

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Sedro-Woolley_-_on_Metcalf_02.jpg/250px-Sedro-Woolley_-_on_Metcalf_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sedro-Woolley_-_on_Metcalf_02.jpg)

Facing southeast at the intersection of Metcalf and Woodworth Streets, downtown Sedro-Woolley, May 2009.

Meanwhile, a fourth town rose nearby when the F&S laid rails on a "[wye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wye_(rail) "Wye (rail)")" that led northeast from Sedro about four and a half miles to [coal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal "Coal") mines. Bennett bought the mines, along with Montana mining financier [Charles X. Larrabee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_X._Larrabee "Charles X. Larrabee"), and they soon sold their interests to [James J. Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_J._Hill "James J. Hill"), owner of the Great Northern. The resulting ore soon turned out to be more suitable for coking coal and a town began there named Cokedale. Cokedale faded in importance when the mine declined and the other towns all merged on December 19, 1898, as Sedro-Woolley.

On July 24, 1911, a fire of unknown origin began near the Fritsch Brothers Hardware store at the northwest corner of Metcalf and Woodworth Streets in the business center of the recently incorporated city.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-9) The fire quickly spread, and all but four structures within the area bounded by Eastern Avenue to the west, Ferry Street to the north, Murdock Street to the east and Woodworth Street to the south were destroyed by the flames. Twenty-five businesses sustained $200,000 in damage. Historic buildings in downtown Sedro-Woolley are now primarily composed of brick as a testament to the disaster.

On May 15, 1922, a circus elephant known as [Tusko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tusko "Tusko") rampaged through the town after it escaped from the traveling [Al G. Barnes Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_G._Barnes_Circus "Al G. Barnes Circus"). He was the largest circus elephant in captivity at the time, measuring 10 feet 2 inches (3.10 m) tall and weighing 7.5 short tons (6,800 kg). Tusko demolished several fences, knocked down telephone poles, and destroyed a [Model T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_T "Model T"). He was chased by local residents for 30 miles (48 km) in the surrounding countryside, and was captured the following morning.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Tusko-10)

After logging and coal-mining declined, the major employers and industries became the nearby [Northern State Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_State_Hospital "Northern State Hospital") (a mental-health facility)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-11) and [Skagit Steel & Iron Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_Steel_&_Iron_Works?action=edit&redlink=1 "Skagit Steel & Iron Works (page does not exist)"), which rose from the back room of a local hardware store to become a major supplier of implements and parts for logging and railroad customers. The firm manufactured machines and parts for the war effort in World War II and artillery shells, starting in 1953. By 1990, the company was gone and the hospital was closed but new industry, including robotics and aerospace, is developing north of town and on the campus of the old hospital.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-13) Current large employers in the town include BYK Construction Inc, Cascades [Job Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_Corps "Job Corps") Center, Janicki Logging & Construction, Janicki Industries, PeaceHealth United General Medical Center District, Rothenbuhler Engineering, the Sedro-Woolley Innovation for Tomorrow (SWIFT) Center, the [Sedro-Woolley School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley_School_District "Sedro-Woolley School District"), [Sedron Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedron_Technologies "Sedron Technologies"), Truck Vault, and the [Upper Skagit Indian Tribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Skagit_Indian_Tribe "Upper Skagit Indian Tribe").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-14)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Government")]

The City of Sedro-Woolley is a non-charter code city that operates under a mayor-council form of government with seven councilmembers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-15) Six councilmembers are elected by wards and one is elected [at-large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-large "At-large").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-16) Each councilmember serves a four-year term.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-17) The mayor is elected at-large every four years and is responsible for the executive functions of the city.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-18) The mayor appoints a city supervisor, subject to confirmation by the city council, who is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the city and oversees the department directors.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-20) The municipal judge is appointed by the mayor, subject to confirmation of the city council, and operates independently of the other branches of government.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-21)

Sedro-Woolley is a full-service city with its own police department, fire department, wastewater treatment plant, solid waste operation, storm water division, street department, community development department, finance department, and parks department and administration. The city maintains a large number of public parks and open spaces such as Hammer Heritage Square in downtown Sedro-Woolley. Riverfront Park situated on the north bank of the Skagit River is the signature park. It consists of nearly 60 acres (240,000 m 2) and includes picnic shelters, baseball fields, RV park, amphitheater, and an off-leash dog park. Every year on the 4th of July the city celebrates with a festive carnival, and hosts the Loggerodeo parade.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 4.35 square miles (11.27 square kilometres), all of it land.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-22) The city is bordered by the [Skagit River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_River "Skagit River") to the south. Sedro-Woolley is also nicknamed the "Gateway to the [North Cascades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Cascades_National_Park "North Cascades National Park")", due to its relative proximity to the National Park to the east.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Climate")]

Sedro-Woolley has a warm-summer [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") (Csb) according to the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") system, but nearly qualifies as having an [oceanic climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") (Cfb) due to its less pronounced drying trend in summer, as compared with elsewhere in western Washington.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Sedro-Woolley had a population of 12,421, 4,562 households, and 2,937 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 2,857.4 inhabitants per square mile (1,103.2 inhabitants per square kilometre). There were 4,759 housing units at an average density of 1,094.8 per square mile (422.7 per square kilometre).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DP-24)

Of the 4,562 households, 34.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 42.6% were married-couple households, 16.9% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 29.7% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 27.1% of all households were made up of individuals and 13.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.72. There was a 4.1% housing vacancy rate, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9% and a rental vacancy rate of 3.9%.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DP-24)

The median age in the city was 34.6 years; 24.6% of residents were under the age of 18, 6.8% were between the ages of 15 and 19, 7.4% were from 20 to 24, 29.1% were from 25 to 44, 20.1% were from 45 to 64, and 15.8% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 48.0% male and 52.0% female, equivalent to 92.4 males per 100 females overall and 90.4 males per 100 females age 18 and over.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DP-24)

97.3% of residents lived in urban areas, while 2.7% lived in rural areas.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DHC-25)

The racial makeup of the city was 91.97% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.25% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 1.59% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.81% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.13% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 3.25% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 2.00% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 7.23% of the population.

There were 3,205 households, out of which 37.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 49.8% were married couples living together, 13.5% had a female householder with no husband present, and 32.1% were non-families. 25.9% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.62 and the average family size was 3.14.

In the city, the age distribution of the population shows 28.8% under the age of 18, 9.2% from 18 to 24, 29.3% from 25 to 44, 18.4% from 45 to 64, and 14.3% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 33 years. For every 100 females, there were 90.3 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 84.8 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $37,914, and the median income for a family was $40,918. Males had a median income of $35,215 versus $23,636 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $16,517. About 10.7% of families and 11.3% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 12.9% of those under age 18 and 16.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Culture")]

Sedro-Woolley is the home of Loggerodeo, an annual festival that takes place near [Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_(United_States) "Independence Day (United States)"). It was established as Sedro's Independence Day celebration in 1886 and renamed to Loggerodeo when the towns merged in 1948.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-27) The festival is the oldest continuous Independence Day celebration in Washington state.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-CDN-Loggerodeo-28) Loggerodeo includes a [carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival "Carnival"), races, arts and crafts, parades, auctions, and logging activities. Since 1996, it has also hosted an invitational [chainsaw carving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainsaw_carving "Chainsaw carving") competition that uses local cedar and attracts sculptors from around the world.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-CDN-Loggerodeo-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-29)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

The [Sedro-Woolley School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley_School_District "Sedro-Woolley School District") operates public schools in the city as well as nearby communities, including [Big Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Lake,_Washington "Big Lake, Washington") and [Clear Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clear_Lake,_Skagit_County,_Washington "Clear Lake, Skagit County, Washington"). The district has one high school ([Sedro-Woolley High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley_High_School "Sedro-Woolley High School")), one middle school, seven elementary schools, and several alternative schooling programs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-30) A [Job Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_Corps "Job Corps") center is also located within the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-31)

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Transportation")]

Sedro-Woolley lies at the intersection of [State Route 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_9 "Washington State Route 9"), a major north–south highway in the Cascade foothills from the [Seattle metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_metropolitan_area "Seattle metropolitan area") to the [Canadian border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93United_States_border "Canada–United States border"), and [State Route 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_20 "Washington State Route 20"), also known as the North Cascades Highway. The two highways travel [concurrently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_(road) "Concurrency (road)") around the city center on Borseth and Moore streets;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-WSDOT-Map-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-33) State Route 20 continues west towards [Interstate 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_5_in_Washington "Interstate 5 in Washington"), a major freeway, and east to North Cascades National Park and [Eastern Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Washington "Eastern Washington").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-WSDOT-Map-32)

[Skagit Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_Transit "Skagit Transit") operates public [bus service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit_bus "Transit bus") within Sedro-Woolley and surrounding communities, including connections to [Skagit Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_Station "Skagit Station") in [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon,_Washington "Mount Vernon, Washington") as well as areas as far east as [Concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete,_Washington "Concrete, Washington").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-34) The agency operates a 20-stall [park-and-ride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park-and-ride "Park-and-ride") lot at West Ferry Street and Cook Road near [State Route 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_20 "Washington State Route 20") that is owned by the [Washington State Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Department_of_Transportation "Washington State Department of Transportation").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-35) Prior to the creation of a new route in 2022, intra-city service within Sedro-Woolley often required a [transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_(public_transport) "Transfer (public transport)") in [Burlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington,_Washington "Burlington, Washington").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-36)

The nearest commercial airport with scheduled passenger service is [Bellingham International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellingham_International_Airport "Bellingham International Airport"), approximately 25 miles (40 km) to the northwest.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Sedro-Woolley** ([/ˌ s iː d r oʊ ˈ w ʊ l i/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_SEE-droh WUUL-ee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")) is a city in [Skagit County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_County,_Washington "Skagit County, Washington"), [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)"), United States. It is part of the [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon,_Washington "Mount Vernon, Washington")–[Anacortes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anacortes,_Washington "Anacortes, Washington"), Washington [Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "Metropolitan Statistical Area") and had a population of 12,421 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). The city is home to the administrative offices of [North Cascades National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Cascades_National_Park "North Cascades National Park"), which lies east of Sedro-Woolley on [State Route 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_20 "Washington State Route 20").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Sedro-Woolley%2C_Washington_%281906%29.jpg/330px-Sedro-Woolley%2C_Washington_%281906%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sedro-Woolley,_Washington_(1906).jpg)

Sedro-Woolley in 1906

Incorporated on December 19, 1898, Sedro-Woolley was formed from neighboring rival towns of Sedro (once known as Bug) and Woolley in [Skagit County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_County "Skagit County"), northwestern Washington, 25 miles (40 kilometres) inland from [Puget Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puget_Sound "Puget Sound"), 40 miles (64 kilometres) south of the border with Canada and 65 miles (105 kilometres) north of [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-5)

Four British bachelors, led by David Batey, homesteaded the area in 1878, the time logjam obstructions were cleared downriver at the site of Mount Vernon.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-6) In 1884–85, Batey built a store and home for the Mortimer Cook family from [Santa Barbara, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara,_California "Santa Barbara, California") where Cook had been mayor for two terms. Cook intended to name his new Pacific Northwest town Bug due to the number of [mosquitoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosquitoes "Mosquitoes") present, but his wife protested along with a handful of other local wives. Cook was already the namesake for the town Cook's Ferry on the Thompson River in [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"). With "Bug" being so unpopular, Cook derived a town name from Spanish; knowing ["cedro"](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedrus "es:Cedrus") was the word for cedar, he replaced one letter to make the name unique, settling on "Sedro".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-7)

Sedro, on the northern banks of the [Skagit River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_River "Skagit River"), proved susceptible to floods. In 1889, [Northern Pacific Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Pacific_Railway "Northern Pacific Railway") developer [Nelson Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Bennett "Nelson Bennett") began laying track from the town of [Fairhaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairhaven,_Washington "Fairhaven, Washington"), 25 miles (40 kilometres) northwest on [Bellingham Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellingham_Bay "Bellingham Bay"), and real estate developer Norman R. Kelley platted a new town of Sedro on high ground a mile northwest of Cook's site. The [Fairhaven and Southern Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairhaven_and_Southern_Railroad "Fairhaven and Southern Railroad") arrived in Sedro on Christmas Eve, 1889, in time for Bennett to receive a performance bonus from the towns at both ends, and a month after Washington became the 42nd state in the Union.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-8)

Within months, two more railroads crossed the F&S roadbed a half mile north of new Sedro, forming a triangle where 11 trains eventually arrived daily. Railroad developer [Philip A. Woolley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley "Philip Woolley") moved his family from [Elgin, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgin,_Illinois "Elgin, Illinois"), to Sedro in December 1899 and bought land around the triangle. He built the Skagit River Lumber & Shingle Mill next to where the railroads crossed and he started his namesake company town there that was based on sales of railroad ties to the three rail companies, including the [Seattle and Northern Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_and_Northern_Railway?action=edit&redlink=1 "Seattle and Northern Railway (page does not exist)") (forerunner of the [Great Northern Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Northern_Railway_(U.S.) "Great Northern Railway (U.S.)")) and the [Northern Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Pacific_Railroad "Northern Pacific Railroad").

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Sedro-Woolley_-_on_Metcalf_02.jpg/250px-Sedro-Woolley_-_on_Metcalf_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sedro-Woolley_-_on_Metcalf_02.jpg)

Facing southeast at the intersection of Metcalf and Woodworth Streets, downtown Sedro-Woolley, May 2009.

Meanwhile, a fourth town rose nearby when the F&S laid rails on a "[wye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wye_(rail) "Wye (rail)")" that led northeast from Sedro about four and a half miles to [coal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal "Coal") mines. Bennett bought the mines, along with Montana mining financier [Charles X. Larrabee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_X._Larrabee "Charles X. Larrabee"), and they soon sold their interests to [James J. Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_J._Hill "James J. Hill"), owner of the Great Northern. The resulting ore soon turned out to be more suitable for coking coal and a town began there named Cokedale. Cokedale faded in importance when the mine declined and the other towns all merged on December 19, 1898, as Sedro-Woolley.

On July 24, 1911, a fire of unknown origin began near the Fritsch Brothers Hardware store at the northwest corner of Metcalf and Woodworth Streets in the business center of the recently incorporated city.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-9) The fire quickly spread, and all but four structures within the area bounded by Eastern Avenue to the west, Ferry Street to the north, Murdock Street to the east and Woodworth Street to the south were destroyed by the flames. Twenty-five businesses sustained $200,000 in damage. Historic buildings in downtown Sedro-Woolley are now primarily composed of brick as a testament to the disaster.

On May 15, 1922, a circus elephant known as [Tusko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tusko "Tusko") rampaged through the town after it escaped from the traveling [Al G. Barnes Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_G._Barnes_Circus "Al G. Barnes Circus"). He was the largest circus elephant in captivity at the time, measuring 10 feet 2 inches (3.10 m) tall and weighing 7.5 short tons (6,800 kg). Tusko demolished several fences, knocked down telephone poles, and destroyed a [Model T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_T "Model T"). He was chased by local residents for 30 miles (48 km) in the surrounding countryside, and was captured the following morning.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Tusko-10)

After logging and coal-mining declined, the major employers and industries became the nearby [Northern State Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_State_Hospital "Northern State Hospital") (a mental-health facility)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-11) and [Skagit Steel & Iron Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_Steel_&_Iron_Works?action=edit&redlink=1 "Skagit Steel & Iron Works (page does not exist)"), which rose from the back room of a local hardware store to become a major supplier of implements and parts for logging and railroad customers. The firm manufactured machines and parts for the war effort in World War II and artillery shells, starting in 1953. By 1990, the company was gone and the hospital was closed but new industry, including robotics and aerospace, is developing north of town and on the campus of the old hospital.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-13) Current large employers in the town include BYK Construction Inc, Cascades [Job Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_Corps "Job Corps") Center, Janicki Logging & Construction, Janicki Industries, PeaceHealth United General Medical Center District, Rothenbuhler Engineering, the Sedro-Woolley Innovation for Tomorrow (SWIFT) Center, the [Sedro-Woolley School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley_School_District "Sedro-Woolley School District"), [Sedron Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedron_Technologies "Sedron Technologies"), Truck Vault, and the [Upper Skagit Indian Tribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Skagit_Indian_Tribe "Upper Skagit Indian Tribe").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-14)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Government")]

The City of Sedro-Woolley is a non-charter code city that operates under a mayor-council form of government with seven councilmembers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-15) Six councilmembers are elected by wards and one is elected [at-large](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/At-large "At-large").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-16) Each councilmember serves a four-year term.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-17) The mayor is elected at-large every four years and is responsible for the executive functions of the city.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-18) The mayor appoints a city supervisor, subject to confirmation by the city council, who is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the city and oversees the department directors.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-20) The municipal judge is appointed by the mayor, subject to confirmation of the city council, and operates independently of the other branches of government.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-21)

Sedro-Woolley is a full-service city with its own police department, fire department, wastewater treatment plant, solid waste operation, storm water division, street department, community development department, finance department, and parks department and administration. The city maintains a large number of public parks and open spaces such as Hammer Heritage Square in downtown Sedro-Woolley. Riverfront Park situated on the north bank of the Skagit River is the signature park. It consists of nearly 60 acres (240,000 m 2) and includes picnic shelters, baseball fields, RV park, amphitheater, and an off-leash dog park. Every year on the 4th of July the city celebrates with a festive carnival, and hosts the Loggerodeo parade.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 4.35 square miles (11.27 square kilometres), all of it land.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-22) The city is bordered by the [Skagit River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_River "Skagit River") to the south. Sedro-Woolley is also nicknamed the "Gateway to the [North Cascades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Cascades_National_Park "North Cascades National Park")", due to its relative proximity to the National Park to the east.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Climate")]

Sedro-Woolley has a warm-summer [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") (Csb) according to the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") system, but nearly qualifies as having an [oceanic climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") (Cfb) due to its less pronounced drying trend in summer, as compared with elsewhere in western Washington.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Sedro-Woolley had a population of 12,421, 4,562 households, and 2,937 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 2,857.4 inhabitants per square mile (1,103.2 inhabitants per square kilometre). There were 4,759 housing units at an average density of 1,094.8 per square mile (422.7 per square kilometre).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DP-24)

Of the 4,562 households, 34.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them; 42.6% were married-couple households, 16.9% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 29.7% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 27.1% of all households were made up of individuals and 13.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.72. There was a 4.1% housing vacancy rate, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9% and a rental vacancy rate of 3.9%.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DP-24)

The median age in the city was 34.6 years; 24.6% of residents were under the age of 18, 6.8% were between the ages of 15 and 19, 7.4% were from 20 to 24, 29.1% were from 25 to 44, 20.1% were from 45 to 64, and 15.8% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 48.0% male and 52.0% female, equivalent to 92.4 males per 100 females overall and 90.4 males per 100 females age 18 and over.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-Census2020DP-24)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-4) there were 10,540 people, 3,995 households, and 2,609 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 2,766.4 inhabitants per square mile (1,068.1 inhabitants per square kilometre). There were 4,303 housing units at an average density of 1,129.4 per square mile (436.1 per square kilometre). The racial makeup of the city was 86.1% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 0.3% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 1.9% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.4% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 6.8% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 3.3% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 14.0% of the population.

There were 3,995 households, of which 36.9% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 43.9% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 14.9% had a female householder with no husband present, 6.5% had a male householder with no wife present, and 34.7% were non-families. 27.0% of all households were made up of individuals, and 10.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.59 and the average family size was 3.12.

The median age in the city was 33.7 years. 27.3% of residents were under the age of 18; 9% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 28.2% were from 25 to 44; 22.7% were from 45 to 64; and 12.7% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 48.3% male and 51.7% female.

[Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 7.23% of the population.

There were 3,205 households, out of which 37.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 49.8% were married couples living together, 13.5% had a female householder with no husband present, and 32.1% were non-families. 25.9% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.6% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.62 and the average family size was 3.14.

In the city, the age distribution of the population shows 28.8% under the age of 18, 9.2% from 18 to 24, 29.3% from 25 to 44, 18.4% from 45 to 64, and 14.3% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 33 years. For every 100 females, there were 90.3 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 84.8 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $37,914, and the median income for a family was $40,918. Males had a median income of $35,215 versus $23,636 for females. About 10.7% of families and 11.3% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 12.9% of those under age 18 and 16.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Culture")]

Sedro-Woolley is the home of Loggerodeo, an annual festival that takes place near [Independence Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_(United_States) "Independence Day (United States)"). It was established as Sedro's Independence Day celebration in 1886 and renamed to Loggerodeo when the towns merged in 1948.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-27) The festival is the oldest continuous Independence Day celebration in Washington state.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-CDN-Loggerodeo-28) Loggerodeo includes a [carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival "Carnival"), races, arts and crafts, parades, auctions, and logging activities. Since 1996, it has also hosted an invitational [chainsaw carving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainsaw_carving "Chainsaw carving") competition that uses local cedar and attracts sculptors from around the world.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-CDN-Loggerodeo-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-29)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

The [Sedro-Woolley School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley_School_District "Sedro-Woolley School District") operates public schools in the city as well as nearby communities, including [Big Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Lake,_Washington "Big Lake, Washington") and [Clear Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clear_Lake,_Skagit_County,_Washington "Clear Lake, Skagit County, Washington"). The district has one high school ([Sedro-Woolley High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley_High_School "Sedro-Woolley High School")), one middle school, seven elementary schools, and several alternative schooling programs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-30) A [Job Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_Corps "Job Corps") center is also located within the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-31)

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sedro-Woolley,_Washington&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Transportation")]

Sedro-Woolley lies at the intersection of [State Route 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_9 "Washington State Route 9"), a major north–south highway in the Cascade foothills from the [Seattle metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_metropolitan_area "Seattle metropolitan area") to the [Canadian border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93United_States_border "Canada–United States border"), and [State Route 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_20 "Washington State Route 20"), also known as the North Cascades Highway. The two highways travel [concurrently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concurrency_(road) "Concurrency (road)") around the city center on Borseth and Moore streets;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-WSDOT-Map-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-33) State Route 20 continues west towards [Interstate 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_5_in_Washington "Interstate 5 in Washington"), a major freeway, and east to North Cascades National Park and [Eastern Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Washington "Eastern Washington").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-WSDOT-Map-32)

[Skagit Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_Transit "Skagit Transit") operates public [bus service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit_bus "Transit bus") within Sedro-Woolley and surrounding communities, including connections to [Skagit Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_Station "Skagit Station") in [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon,_Washington "Mount Vernon, Washington") as well as areas as far east as [Concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete,_Washington "Concrete, Washington").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-34) The agency operates a 20-stall [park-and-ride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park-and-ride "Park-and-ride") lot at West Ferry Street and Cook Road near [State Route 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Route_20 "Washington State Route 20") that is owned by the [Washington State Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Department_of_Transportation "Washington State Department of Transportation").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-35) Prior to the creation of a new route in 2022, intra-city service within Sedro-Woolley often required a [transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_(public_transport) "Transfer (public transport)") in [Burlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington,_Washington "Burlington, Washington").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley#cite_note-36)

The nearest commercial airport with scheduled passenger service is [Bellingham International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellingham_International_Airport "Bellingham International Airport"), approximately 25 miles (40 km) to the northwest.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Philip Woolley** (February 17, 1831 – June 12, 1912) was a [Canadian American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_American "Canadian American") businessman for whom the city of Sedro-Woolley, [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)"), is partly named.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Philip_Woolley&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Philip Woolley was born in [Malone, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malone,_New_York "Malone, New York"), to an American father and Canadian mother.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley#cite_note-historyink-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Philip_Woolley&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Woolley moved to [Russell, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell,_Ontario "Russell, Ontario") in the 1850s, where he worked as a [lumberjack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumberjack "Lumberjack") and opened a [general store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_store "General store"). In 1867 he relocated his family to [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan") and, later, to [Elgin, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgin,_Illinois "Elgin, Illinois"). Building on his experience as a lumberjack and salesman in Ontario, Woolley began selling timber for railroad crossties to the Chicago & Alton Railway.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley#cite_note-historyink-1)

In 1889 Woolley again moved, this time to [Washington state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_state "Washington state"), in hope of growing his railway contracting business by taking advantage of the expanding [Northern Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Pacific_Railroad "Northern Pacific Railroad"), which had just established a terminus in [Tacoma, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacoma,_Washington "Tacoma, Washington"). Woolley settled in Sedro, Washington, in [Skagit County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skagit_County "Skagit County"), purchasing 84 acres of land just outside the town limits at a location where he felt the expanding rail lines would cross. Meanwhile, with his sons, he began constructing the Skagit River Lumber & Shingle Mill on his newly acquired property, growing his acreage into a company town named Woolley. In 1898, the two towns were merged as [Sedro-Woolley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley,_Washington "Sedro-Woolley, Washington").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley#cite_note-3)

Woolley continued to enjoy business success in later life, supplying material to the [Seaboard Air Line Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seaboard_Air_Line_Railroad "Seaboard Air Line Railroad") and taking up part-time residence in [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") to service his new client.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley#cite_note-historyink-1)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Philip_Woolley&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Woolley married Catherine Loucks of Ottawa on January 23, 1857. They had at least five children. Woolley died at his home on Woodworth Street in Sedro-Woolley in 1912.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Woolley#cite_note-historyink-1)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American photographer (1869–1945)

**Darius Kinsey** (1869–1945) was a photographer active in western [Washington state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") from 1890 to 1940. He is best known for his large-format images of loggers and phases of the region's lumber industry. He also photographed locomotives and landscapes and (especially early in his career) did studio work.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

Kinsey, born in [Maryville, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryville,_Missouri "Maryville, Missouri"), moved to [Snoqualmie, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoqualmie,_Washington "Snoqualmie, Washington"), where he took up photography in 1890.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Kinsey_log_house.JPG/250px-Kinsey_log_house.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kinsey_log_house.JPG)

Cedar stump house, 1901

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Logging_in_Washington_state_by_Darius_Kinsey.jpg/250px-Logging_in_Washington_state_by_Darius_Kinsey.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Logging_in_Washington_state_by_Darius_Kinsey.jpg)

_Spruce_, c. 1906

He worked as an itinerant photographer for several years, until meeting Tabitha May Pritts at [Nooksack, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nooksack,_Washington "Nooksack, Washington"). The couple married in 1896. The following year, they set up a photo studio in [Sedro-Woolley, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley,_Washington "Sedro-Woolley, Washington"). They had two children, Dorothea and Darius, Jr.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

In 1906, the couple moved to [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"). Darius gave up studio work and focused instead on the lumber industry and scenic photography. Tabitha developed the negatives and made the prints, which were sent back to the logging camps and sold to the loggers. Darius used an 11" X 14" Empire State view camera with a custom made tripod that could extend twelve feet high. He used glass plates until 1914, when he switched to film.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

In 1920 Kinsey photographed the [Giant Cedar Stump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Cedar_Stump "Giant Cedar Stump") near [Arlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Washington "Arlington, Washington").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-KinseyPhoto-2)

After falling from a stump in October, 1940, Darius was forced to give up photography. He spent the last five years of his life sorting and organizing his negatives. He died in 1945 and is buried with his wife in Nooksack.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

The major collection of his work is held by the [Whatcom Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatcom_Museum "Whatcom Museum") in [Bellingham, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellingham,_Washington "Bellingham, Washington"). The University of Washington Libraries also has a collection of his work.

Darius' brother [Clark Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_Kinsey "Clark Kinsey") was also a photographer of early 20th Century logging in Washington.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American photographer (1869–1945)

**Darius Kinsey** (1869–1945) was a photographer active in western [Washington state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)") from 1890 to 1940. He is best known for his large-format images of loggers and phases of the region's lumber industry. He also photographed locomotives and landscapes and (especially early in his career) did studio work.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

Kinsey, born in [Maryville, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryville,_Missouri "Maryville, Missouri"), moved to [Snoqualmie, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoqualmie,_Washington "Snoqualmie, Washington"), where he took up photography in 1890.

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Kinsey_log_house.JPG/250px-Kinsey_log_house.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kinsey_log_house.JPG)

Cedar stump house, 1901

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Logging_in_Washington_state_by_Darius_Kinsey.jpg/250px-Logging_in_Washington_state_by_Darius_Kinsey.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Logging_in_Washington_state_by_Darius_Kinsey.jpg)

_Spruce_, c. 1906

He worked as an itinerant photographer for several years, until meeting Tabitha May Pritts at [Nooksack, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nooksack,_Washington "Nooksack, Washington"). The couple married in 1896. The following year, they set up a photo studio in [Sedro-Woolley, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedro-Woolley,_Washington "Sedro-Woolley, Washington"). They had two children, Dorothea and Darius, Jr.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

In 1906, the couple moved to [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"). Darius gave up studio work and focused instead on the lumber industry and scenic photography. Tabitha developed the negatives and made the prints, which were sent back to the logging camps and sold to the loggers. Darius used an 11" X 14" Empire State view camera with a custom made tripod that could extend twelve feet high. He used glass plates until 1914, when he switched to film.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

In 1920 Kinsey photographed the [Giant Cedar Stump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Cedar_Stump "Giant Cedar Stump") near [Arlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington,_Washington "Arlington, Washington").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-KinseyPhoto-2)

After falling from a stump in October, 1940, Darius was forced to give up photography. He spent the last five years of his life sorting and organizing his negatives. He died in 1945 and is buried with his wife in Nooksack.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_Kinsey#cite_note-Chronicle-1)

The major collection of his work is held by the [Whatcom Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatcom_Museum "Whatcom Museum") in [Bellingham, Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellingham,_Washington "Bellingham, Washington"). The University of Washington Libraries also has a collection of his work.

Darius' brother [Clark Kinsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_Kinsey "Clark Kinsey") was also a photographer of early 20th Century logging in Washington.

A **hotel manager**, **hotelier**, **motel manager** or **lodging manager** is a person who manages the operation of a [hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel "Hotel"), [motel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motel "Motel"), [resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort "Resort"), or other [lodging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodging "Lodging")-related establishment.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-1) Management of a [hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel "Hotel") operation includes, but is not limited to: [management of hotel staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_management "Performance management"), [business management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management "Management"), upkeep and sanitary standards of hotel facilities, [guest satisfaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customer_satisfaction "Customer satisfaction") and [customer service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customer_service "Customer service"), [marketing management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketing_management "Marketing management"), [sales management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sales_management "Sales management"), [revenue management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenue_management "Revenue management"), [financial accounting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_accounting "Financial accounting"), [purchasing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purchasing "Purchasing"), and other functions. The title "hotel manager" or "hotelier" often refers to the hotel's [general manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") who serves as a hotel's head executive, though their duties and responsibilities vary depending on the hotel's size, purpose, and expectations from ownership. The hotel's general manager is often supported by subordinate department managers that are responsible for individual departments and key functions of the hotel operations.

## Hotel management structure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Hotel management structure")]

The size and complexity of a hotel management organizational structure varies significantly depending on the size, features, and function of the hotel or resort.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-Bardi2006-2) A small hotel operation normally may consist of a small core management team consisting of a hotel manager and a few key department supervisors who directly handle day-to-day operations. On the other hand, a large full-service hotel or resort complex often operates more similarly to a large [corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporation "Corporation") with an executive board headed by the [general manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") and consisting of key directors serving as heads of individual hotel departments. Each department at the large hotel or resort complex may normally consist of subordinate line-level managers and supervisors who handle day-to-day operations.

### Example for small/limited service hotel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Example for small/limited service hotel")]

A typical organizational chart for a small low-rise hotel operation may resemble the following:

_Hotel manager reports to regional director and/or ownership/investors_

*   [General manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager")

 ** Guest service manager (front of house)
 ** Housekeeping manager
 ** Chief engineer
 ** Sales & marketing manager
 ** Food & beverage manager
 ** Account manager
 Administrative functions for a small-scale hotel such as accounting, payroll, and human resources may normally be handled by a centralized corporate office or solely by the hotel manager. Additional auxiliary functions such as security may be handled by third-party vendor services contracted by the hotel on an as-needed basis. Hotel management is necessary to implement standard operating procedures and actions as well as handling day-to-day operations.

### Example for a motel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Example for a motel")]

A typical motel organizational chart[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-MotelCoach-4) may resemble the following:

*   Motel Manager

 ** Restaurant Manager or Chef
 ** Housekeeping Manager
 ** Housekeepers
 ** Maintenance is completed by the on-site manager, maintenance officer or a tradesman.
 ** Receptionist
In a small motel, the motel manager's role is hands-on, often with daily engagement in housekeeping, maintenance and reception.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-MotelCoach-4)

## Typical qualifications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Typical qualifications")]

The background and training required varies by the type of management position, size of operation, and duties involved. Industry experience has proven to be a basic qualification for nearly any management occupation within the lodging industry. A [BS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BS_degree "BS degree") and a [MS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MS_degree "MS degree") degree in [Hospitality Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospitality_management_studies "Hospitality management studies")/or an equivalent [Business degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_degree "Business degree") is often strongly preferred by most employers in the industry but not always required.

A higher level graduate degree may be desired for a [general manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") type position, but is often not required with sufficient management experience and industry tenure. A graduate degree may however be required for a higher level corporate executive position or above such as a Regional Vice President who oversees multiple hotel properties and general managers.

## Working conditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Working conditions")]

Hotel managers are generally exposed to long shifts that include late hours, weekends, and holidays due to the [24-hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24-hour "24-hour") operation of a hotel. The common workplace environment in hotels is fast-paced, with high levels of interaction with guests, employees, investors, and other managers.

Upper management consisting of senior managers, department heads, and [general managers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") may sometimes enjoy a more desirable work schedule consisting of a more traditional [business day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_day "Business day") with occasional weekends and holidays off.

Depending on the size of the hotel, a typical hotel manager's day may include assisting with operational duties, managing employee performance, handling dissatisfied guests, managing work schedules, purchasing supplies, interviewing potential job candidates, conducting physical walks and inspections of the hotel facilities and public areas, and additional duties. These duties may vary each day depending on the needs of the property. The manager's responsibility also includes knowing about all current local events as well as the events being held on the hotel property. Managers are often required to attend regular department meetings, management meetings, training seminars for professional development, and additional functions. A hotel/casino property may require additional duties regarding special events being held on property for casino complimentary guests.

### 2020 coronavirus pandemic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020 coronavirus pandemic")]

Working conditions were increasingly difficult during the [2020 coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). One CEO of a major hotel owner, [Monty Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monty_Bennett "Monty Bennett") of Ashford Inc., told CBS News that he had to lay off or furlough 95% of his 7,000 U.S. workers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-5) To save money, hotel management are compelled to reduce all discretionary operational and capital costs, and review or postpone maintenance and other capital investments whenever possible.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-6) By the second week of the major outbreak of the virus in the U.S., the industry asked Congress for $250 billion in bailouts for owners and employees because of financial setbacks and mass layoffs.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-7)

## Salary expectations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Salary expectations")]

The median annual wage in 2015 of the 48,400 lodging managers in the United States was $49,720.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-autogenerated1-8)

A **hotel manager**, **hotelier**, **motel manager** or **lodging manager** is a person who manages the operation of a [hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel "Hotel"), [motel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motel "Motel"), [resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort "Resort"), or other [lodging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodging "Lodging")-related establishment.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-1) Management of a [hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel "Hotel") operation includes, but is not limited to: [management of hotel staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_management "Performance management"), [business management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management "Management"), upkeep and sanitary standards of hotel facilities, [guest satisfaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customer_satisfaction "Customer satisfaction") and [customer service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Customer_service "Customer service"), [marketing management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketing_management "Marketing management"), [sales management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sales_management "Sales management"), [revenue management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenue_management "Revenue management"), [financial accounting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_accounting "Financial accounting"), [purchasing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purchasing "Purchasing"), and other functions. The title "hotel manager" or "hotelier" often refers to the hotel's [general manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") who serves as a hotel's head executive, though their duties and responsibilities vary depending on the hotel's size, purpose, and expectations from ownership. The hotel's general manager is often supported by subordinate department managers that are responsible for individual departments and key functions of the hotel operations.

## Hotel management structure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Hotel management structure")]

The size and complexity of a hotel management organizational structure varies significantly depending on the size, features, and function of the hotel or resort.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-Bardi2006-2) A small hotel operation normally may consist of a small core management team consisting of a hotel manager and a few key department supervisors who directly handle day-to-day operations. On the other hand, a large full-service hotel or resort complex often operates more similarly to a large [corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporation "Corporation") with an executive board headed by the [general manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") and consisting of key directors serving as heads of individual hotel departments. Each department at the large hotel or resort complex may normally consist of subordinate line-level managers and supervisors who handle day-to-day operations.

### Example for small/limited service hotel

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Example for small/limited service hotel")]

A typical organizational chart for a small low-rise hotel operation may resemble the following:

_Hotel manager reports to regional director and/or ownership/investors_

*   [General manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager")

 ** Guest service manager (front of house)
 ** Housekeeping manager
 ** Chief engineer
 ** Sales & marketing manager
 ** Food & beverage manager
 ** Account manager
 Administrative functions for a small-scale hotel such as accounting, payroll, and human resources may normally be handled by a centralized corporate office or solely by the hotel manager. Additional auxiliary functions such as security may be handled by third-party vendor services contracted by the hotel on an as-needed basis. Hotel management is necessary to implement standard operating procedures and actions as well as handling day-to-day operations.

## Typical qualifications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Typical qualifications")]

The background and training required varies by the type of management position, size of operation, and duties involved. Industry experience has proven to be a basic qualification for nearly any management occupation within the lodging industry. A [BS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BS_degree "BS degree") and a [MS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MS_degree "MS degree") degree in [Hospitality Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hospitality_management_studies "Hospitality management studies")/or an equivalent [Business degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_degree "Business degree") is often strongly preferred by most employers in the industry but not always required.

A higher level graduate degree may be desired for a [general manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") type position, but is often not required with sufficient management experience and industry tenure. A graduate degree may however be required for a higher level corporate executive position or above such as a Regional Vice President who oversees multiple hotel properties and general managers.

## Working conditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Working conditions")]

Hotel managers are generally exposed to long shifts that include late hours, weekends, and holidays due to the [24-hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24-hour "24-hour") operation of a hotel. The common workplace environment in hotels is fast-paced, with high levels of interaction with guests, employees, investors, and other managers.

Upper management consisting of senior managers, department heads, and [general managers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Manager "General Manager") may sometimes enjoy a more desirable work schedule consisting of a more traditional [business day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_day "Business day") with occasional weekends and holidays off.

Depending on the size of the hotel, a typical hotel manager's day may include assisting with operational duties, managing employee performance, handling dissatisfied guests, managing work schedules, purchasing supplies, interviewing potential job candidates, conducting physical walks and inspections of the hotel facilities and public areas, and additional duties. These duties may vary each day depending on the needs of the property. The manager's responsibility also includes knowing about all current local events as well as the events being held on the hotel property. Managers are often required to attend regular department meetings, management meetings, training seminars for professional development, and additional functions. A hotel/casino property may require additional duties regarding special events being held on property for casino complimentary guests.

### 2020 coronavirus pandemic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hotel_manager&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020 coronavirus pandemic")]

Working conditions were increasingly difficult during the [2020 coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). One CEO of a major hotel owner, [Monty Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monty_Bennett "Monty Bennett") of Ashford Inc., told CBS News that he had to lay off or furlough 95% of his 7,000 U.S. workers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-5) To save money, hotel management are compelled to reduce all discretionary operational and capital costs, and review or postpone maintenance and other capital investments whenever possible.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-6) By the second week of the major outbreak of the virus in the U.S., the industry asked Congress for $250 billion in bailouts for owners and employees because of financial setbacks and mass layoffs.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotelier#cite_note-7)
